label: paragraph_title
text: LOCAL STRIKE:

label: text
text: NOT SPREADING

label: text
text: Government's

label: text
text: Of To-day's strike news the best feature is that the trouble has not spread with the rapidity which some expected.

label: text
text: Hardly any new line of labour is affected. On the other hand, there is talk about the general rank and file having been granted permission by the “United Hong Kong Labour Council,” which, apparently, is subservient to higher authorities in Canton, to any on till after the Dragon Boat Festival (5th day of the 5th moon), which is the day after tomorrow.

label: text
text: As will be readily seen, the strike has affected the "China Mail". To-day's issue is considerably reduced in size but publication will continue as long as is humanly possible. Subscribers not receiving their copies will assist by calling for same or obtaining them on the streets.

label: text
text: Domestic servants are still leaving and the exodus of Chinese of all classes continues. One estimate puts the number of workers, and their families, who have left in the first three days, at 20,000.

label: text
text: Those Government notifications regarding rewards and payment to those killed or injured, have borne effects as will be seen from the arrests and convictions reported to-day.

label: text
text: Even under rksome conditions and inconvenience, residents are arerying on cheerfully and deter-medly.

label: text
text: Tickets of Volunteers including the Scottish Company in their kilts to co-operating with the Police in controlling the streets. No untoward incident to disturb the peace has been reported so far.

label: text
text: The anti-British shipping strike has widened in scope, as has the stoppage of domestic servants.

label: text
text: The shipping position now amounts almost to a deadlock and the ships of Messrs. Butterfield and Swire are ordered to Kowloon Bay immediately they discharge their cargo. Nine have so far been thus affected, their crews having come out almost to a man.

label: text
text: The crews of the boats of Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co. have not, as has been reported, left their work as one man. This applies in the case of one boat bound for Bangkok's manned entirely by Southern Chinese, but the Northern Chinese seamen are so far almost unaffected and although several boats have considerably depleted crews; others have almost their full supply.

label: text
text:
On enquiry at the local offices of Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd., the “China Mail” was informed that they were doing their best under difficult circumstances.
It is impossible to forecast future shipping developments until the attitude of the stdevdores (who are at present working normally) is known, also the effect of the restriction on exports.

label: text
text:
Advantage is being taken of the respite so that ships can undergo docking. A previous arrangement will use the Indo-Uthna vessels to go into Cosmopolitan Dock would have been carried out irrespective of the strike.
It was reported this morning that the coasting steamer Apoey had been affected but subsequently it was stated that a crew would be found this afternoon.
Of the clearances at the Harbour Office this morning, there were very few for British steamers, those flying the British flag but owned by Chinese, such as the s.s. Mathilde, not being involved. A good many other foreign vessels were cleared this morning.

label: text
text:
Hotels and Cafes.
The position at Hotels, Cafes, etc., is very much the same as yesterday except that the service is more efficient now that emergency arrangements have had a chance to settle down.
The Hongkong Hotel has been compelled to supplement the emergency staff with foreign assistants who arrived this morning from Shanghai. There was a large queue waiting for tables at the grille room today, but the request of the management has been acceded to on all sides that patience should be exercised and customers co-operate wherever possible to facilitate the working of the arrangements made for meeting the present situation.
Caldwell, Macgregor & Co. inform the “China Mail” that they have foreseen the crisis and have ample stocks of wines, spirits and beers for the emergency.

label: text
text: Four Chinese were charged at the Central Magistracy this morning for having in their possession seditious literature. Two of the men were sentenced to ten months' hard labour each, one to nine months, and other to six months. The fourth man, who also had with him some meal tickets issued by a union of cook-boys and houseboys, was in addition fined $500, or a further three months.

label: text
text: Trespassers Convicted

label: text
text: Two out of the three Northern Chinese charged at the Kowloon Magistracy yesterday with trespassing at Holt's wharf were sentenced to two months' hard labour each this morning. The third man, who volunteered to produce evidence that he went there to see a friend, was discharged.

label: text
text:
Bank Deposit Order.
Under the provisions of the Emergency Regulations Ordinance, the "Government Gazette" announces that the following order was made in the Executive Council yesterday:

label: text
text: The Banks named in the fellowing schedule are prohibited from paying out to any depositor a sum larger than ten per centum of the amount standing to his credit with them, except under licence from the Colonial Secretary.

label: text
text: Should any such Bank be unwilling to comply with this regulation, it is hereby permitted to suspend business until the regulation is withdrawn:—

Effect of Embora.

label: text
text: Additional Revenue Officers have been appointed and it is doubtful if foodstuffs can be smuggled away.

label: text
text: Yesterday, a tremendous quantity of Canton silver subsidiary coins was sent to Macao where there was a panic, a rumour starting that there would be a boycott on British banknotes. By this morning rice in the Portuguese Colony had gone up as much as $5 a bag but otherwise, the position is returning to normal.

label: text
text: A number of lots of foodstuffs intended for export, some possibly unwittingly, were stopped.

label: text
text: The activities of the Dairy Farm and the Peak Store were carried on as usual this morning. Only one Chinese was on duty, but quite a number of ladies and men assisted as volunteers, being kept extremely busy. It may seem too early to judge of the cash system by the first morning's work, but it certainly did not make for the acceleration of business. It was the opinion of the volunteer helpers that customers could have been attended to in a quarter of the time had the passbook system been in vogue or even a duplicate docket system.

label: text
text: All strange Chinese visiting Peak houses are intercepted by men of the Regiment, whom they have to satisfy as to their bends before being allowed to proceed.

label: text
text: Subscribers to the "China Mail" not receiving their copies during the strike will assist by calling for game or obtaining them on the street.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hospital and Ambulance.

label: text
text:
Mr. E. Ralphs is in charge of Hospital, V.A.D. and, Ambulance services. Those wishing to assist are requested to communicate with him at the Education Office, stating what particular duties they wish to perform.
With regard to supplies of fresh milk, the Dairy Farm requests supporters to bring cleaned bottles as this will facilitate distribution.

label: text
text: The Hongkong Club boys have given notice, and the members will carry out the work themselves.

label: text
text: There are in the Colony a considerable number of Filipino and Portuguese workers who can be employed for unskilled or semi-skilled work.

label: paragraph_title
text: Smaller Businesses.

label: text
text: Small business houses are in many cases at an absolute standstill and larger ones report "little doing." This has enabled Volunteer employees to turn out almost en masse to do the 24 hours' duty which will probably fall to the lot of most. This consists of night and day patrols (acting in conjunction with the police) and presence at Volunteer Headquarters in case of an emergency.

label: text
text:
St. Stephen's College (Boys' and Girls') also St. Paul's College (Boys') have joined the Government Schools and Diocesan School in closing for the present. Students who put in an appearance this morning were informed of the decision by the head masters. It is reported that St. Paul's (Girls') College is the only College to be still in session.
At Belilios Girls' School many of the Chinese girls have not turned up. The remainder have been told by the head mistress not to come back till further notice.

label: text
text: A meeting of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce was held yesterday.

label: text
text: The Hon. Mr. Chow Shou-son detailed an interview which he and the Hon Mr. R. H. Kotewall had with H.E. the Governor. He informed the meeting that he had an assurance from the Government that all will be treated alike and be afforded full protection. There was no fear of a shortage of provisions, water or any other necessities, and the Government will also maintain the electric lighting and ferry services.

label: text
text: A discussion followed in regard to food supplies, and it was decided that all the Chinese should work together. Arrangements for distribution of food to the Chinese was also discussed.

label: text
text: Profiteers have not been slow to take advantage of the situation. As the pork butchers are absent, prices of pork have risen several times over. Higher rates have also been asked for other commodities but it is felt that as soon as the distribution arrangements are put in hand, no hardship need be entailed.

label: text
text: Many families were still hoarding up supplies yesterday and this morning and cargo coolies are working overtime.

label: text
text: The price of rice has also gone up and until distribution is running smoothly, it will be difficult to check possibles. At any rate, the food export embargo will have its effect very shortly.

label: text
text: Beef, vegetables and salt-water fish were available in the markets this morning but there were tendencies all round of putting prices up.

label: text
text: Attempts having been made to intimidate the crews of three Java-China-Japan Line steamers, the Captains promptly slipped moorings and went off to Stonecutters Island where they awaited clearance papers and then steamed out of the harbour.

label: text
text:
A secret strike executive has been formed, reported to be under the patronage of the Canton Government, demanding, interalis, the abolition of racial discrimination, the right of workers to elect Chinese members of the Legislative Council, an eight-hour day and abolition of child labour. The Government has issued a proclamation of Emergency Regulations, providing censorship of telegrams and letters, control of premises, vehicles, fuel and food stuffs, also the licensing of export of foodstuffs, gold, silver coin and bank notes.
There is a run on Chinese banks

text: SHANGHAI TROUBLE.

label: paragraph_title
text: ANTI-FOREIGN BOYCOTT PROPOSALS

label: text
text: SCOPE OF ENQUIRY

label: text
text: Latest Developments From All Sources.

label: text
text: Little fresh news has arrived in connection with the trouble at Shanghai. At Home, the Premier has turned down a suggestion for Trade Union inquiry.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hankow Proposals

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: Lf n 1

label: text
text: Hankow, June 22. The situation is quiet.

label: text
text: Arrangements by the agitators for the Dragon Boat Festival include the projected British boycott, comprising (1) refusal of all British banknotes and withdrawal of all money from British Banks, (2) not buying, not selling British goods in future, (3) all relations with British institutions, whether business or religious to be severed; a monster demonstration also arranging Thursday with another Friday and a speech day on June 28 as a grand finale.

label: text
text: Whether Tupan Hsiao Yao-nan will sanction these proceedings is not yet known.

label: paragraph_title
text: Scope of Inquiry.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Serifone.)

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, replying to Mr. Hayes, Mr. Austen Chamberlain, "the Secretary for Foreign Affairs, said it might be assumed that the enquiry at Shanghai would cover the questions of the time allowed to elapse between the warning to the crowd and the order to shoot, and the Powers possessed by the International Authorities in dealing with street processions, but the British Charge de Affaires at Peking was being instructed to make sure it did so.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, replying to Mr. Rennie Smith, Mr. Stanley Baldwin, the Premier, rejected the suggestion that a Trade Union delegation be appointed to investigate the industrial conditions at Shanghai.

label: paragraph_title
text: Paris Incident.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: According to the “Petit Parisien,” the Chinese raiders at the Chinese Legation accepted the Minister’s offer to sign a safe conduct for them and abandoned the idea of holding a street demonstration. They left at the Legation placards which were to be used for the purpose of the demonstration and inscribed “China for the Chinese,” “down with International Imperialism,” etc. The Communist organ, “Humanite,” refers to the raiders as “our comrades.”

label: text
text: The raiders at the Chinese Legation were, apparently, nearly all workmen, respectably dressed and seemingly, hailing from all provinces of China. The Legation is of the opinion the motives of the raiders were patriotic, on the ground of Chinese Diplomatic officers not taking active enough steps to submit the Chinese demands of emancipation from foreign control to Governments to which they were accredited. Legation officers deprecate the methods adopted as harmful to the Chinese cause and emphasised

label: paragraph_title
text: Earlier News.

label: text
text: In addition to Mr. G. M. Young's appointment as Controller of Labour with headquarters at the City Hall, the following were made effective yesterday:—Mr. N. L. Smith to be Food Controller, Mr. C. McL. Messer to be Controller of Transport, Mr. M. J. Breeh to be Censor.

label: text
text:
As notified elsewhere, the June share settlement for to-day has been postponed and the two stock exchanges have been closed temporarily.
The Chinese and native banks having been given permission, no run on them will be effective. Chinese business houses have also found an amicable arrangement for holding out till the crisis is over.
Government Schools affected by students staying away are closed till further notice. Several other schools have suspended studies owing to their scholars joining the strike movement.
that the raiders in no wise represent the whole of the Chinese colony in Paris, but rather the extremist group, affiliated to extremists in China. The Legation suspects non-Chinese elements are behind the coup which, evidently, was most carefully planned and hinted at the possible hand of Moscow again working. The French Police are inquiring into the matter and interesting revelations are possible.

label: text
text: The enquiry has opened against Cheng Kong-ching, arrested in connection with the Legation raid yesterday. The Police are believed to know the names of some of the ringleaders who are probably members of the Chinese Communist organisation, whose headquarters are in the suburb of La Garenne Colombes.

label: text
text: Later.

label: paragraph_title
text: Earlier Cables.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Shanghai, June 22.

label: text
text: Mr. Akaike, former Superintendent General of the Tokyo Police, and a member of the House of Peers, and Mr. Hochizuki, manager of the Kenseikai, arrived in Shanghai to-day. They are unofficially inquiring into the strike.

label: text
text: Four American destroyers reached Woosung from Chefoo, where the situation is easier.

label: text
text: Reports from Swatow, Amoy and Foochow state the situation is not bad. Demonstrations are continuing, but the strikes are not spreading. The situation at the Yangtze ports is unchanged.

label: text
text: A message from Wuhu states that coolies assaulted the Japanese Salt Commissioner whom the Chinese police thereupon arrested and charged with being in possession of arms.

label: text
text: A cable from Hoihow states that there is great unrest at Hainan Island, where there has been an anti-foreign agitation.

label: text
text: The President McKinley and the Oostkerk are omitting their usual call at Hongkong, owing to the strike. The former sails for Shanghai direct, on Tuesday.

label: text
text: The situation ashore and afloat is unchanged.

label: text
text: Mr. Yu Ya-ching, Chairman of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, in a statement in the vernacular papers, indignantly denies the alleged acceptance of a bribe. He adds that he is undaunted by such an unjust accusation and will continue to work in the interests of the nation.

label: text
text: The strained relations between the students and the Chamber of Commerce are revealed in the extremist propaganda partly directed against the Chamber, while the moderate strikers suggest re-opening if the shops and banks adequately contribute to the strike.

label: text
text: Chinese reports state that Chang Hsueh-liang will shortly declare martial law in the districts adjoining the Settlement.

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, June 22.

label: text
text: Chang Hsueh-liang sent northward this afternoon one company of his soldiers. Arrangements are being made to send the rest of his troops—known as the north-eastern training corps—after him. label: text
text: A student demonstration in the native city, this afternoon fell flat. There were speeches, but no procession and no disturbances.

label: text
text: Three Chinese have been arrested in connection with the armed robbery at 154, Gonnaught Road, on Saturday afternoon when seven men secured a haul of $15,000.
